newsitem.title: USA: Japan lifts trade barriers on vitamins, U.S. says.
newsitem.headline: Japan lifts trade barriers on vitamins, U.S. says.

text.p: Japan has agreed to lift trade barriers on a range of vitamins and dietary supplements, which would give substantially greater market access to U.S. firms, the Commerce Department said on Friday.
Japan issued regulations April 1 adopting a long-standing U.S. request to regulate vitamins and supplements as foods rather than as drugs, the department said in a statement.

Vitamins A, B1, B2, C, D and E and niacin are covered by the new regulation. Restrictions on an additional six -- vitamins B6, B12, and K and pantothenic acid, folic acid and biotin -- were also lifted for low doses.
Previous regulations were very restrictive, making the Japanese market too costly and difficult for most foreign supplement firms to participate in, the statement said.
The regulations result from years of negotiations with the United States, the department said.
